Alex Chen: Quick question — need to give a contractor read access to prod logs for a one-off debug. What's our least-privileged pattern here?

Rita Morales: Prefer a log sink -> BigQuery view with column-level masking, not project-level roles. Safer for PII. For an emergency debug we can do ephemeral JIT console access. See https://go/redwood-security/logs-redaction for the patterns.

Alex Chen: They only need request IDs and error stacks, absolutely no user emails or full payloads. Would granting roles/logging.viewer at the project be a no-go?

Mike S: Project-level roles/logging.viewer will expose raw log entries including payloads. Recommended flow: create a sink to BQ, transform/redact offending fields, expose a view that selects masked columns. Example masking in SQL: 
```sql
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(timestamp) AS ts,
  REGEXP_REPLACE(jsonPayload.user_email, r"[^@\\s]+", "***") AS user_email_masked,
  jsonPayload.request_id AS request_id,
  jsonPayload.error_stack AS error_stack
FROM `redwood-prod.logging_sink_dataset._raw_logs`
WHERE severity >= "ERROR"
```

Alex Chen: Nice. Can someone paste the quick gcloud command to bind a temporary viewer with an IAM Condition (time-limited) in case we need console access as fallback?

Rita Morales: You can use IAM Conditions. Example (replace timestamps/member):
```bash
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod \\
  --member="user:contractor@example.com" \\
  --role="roles/logging.viewer" \\
  --condition="title=TempDebug,expression=request.time < timestamp('2026-05-01T16:30:00Z'),description=2-hour debug window"
```
Keep in mind the condition expression must use UTC timestamp and be set to the end of the allowed window.

Alex Chen: Ok — plan: I'll create the sink + masked view and then open an access request for a 2-hour window if the contractor needs console traces. Contractor is in the SSO group contractor-sre@redwood.com. Any objections to that approach?

sec-bot: Access request created: AR-2026-433. Approvers: Rita Morales, Mike S.

Mike S: Approve. Quick note: avoid inventing a new custom role right now unless necessary — bucket the permissions to BQ view access + logging sink writer identity.

Eva K: If you use BQ sink, remember to grant dataset-level access to the view only: `roles/bigquery.dataViewer` on the dataset containing the view. Do NOT grant datasetOwner. Also check billing alerts for increased export size.

Alex Chen: I'll set up the sink + view, grant the view to the SSO group for 2 hours via the access request, and paste the redaction SQL for review. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Rita Morales: Flag: remind me to review the sink filter & SQL before you enable the dataset access. I can approve the redaction rule quick.

Alex Chen: Will do — pinging once it's ready.
